In the care of Gordon Elliott, she's a half-sister to Group 3 winner Iveagh Gardens. Better known for his handling of point-to-pointers, Pat Turley is represented by Double Order. From the family of Kim Muir winner Daily Present, this Order Of St George bay warrants respect with Toni Quail aboard. Others for the shortlist are Georginas Jet, who is a half-sister to dual bumper winner Carrarea, and the Gavin Cromwell-trained Annarubyrose.

Both the Aidan O'Brien-trained Kansas and Jessica Harrington's Taiyi are newcomers worthy of consideration, especially if the market speaks in their favour.

selections.comment: TOMARLO should be all the better after his recent third at Tipperary. Noticeably weak in the market, the David Marnane-trained three-year-old travelled into the race strongly before weakening inside the final furlong. Likely to be much straighter, the son of Iffraaj has the potential to be a lot better than a mark of 67. Nicely drawn towards the stands side, the gelding should be capable of making his presence felt against more exposed opposition. Navan winner Beano Power should be competitive off an 8lb higher rating. Eddie Lynam has few peers when it comes to training sprinters, so further improvement would not surprise. Sarahmae, who beat the selection last time, is another with leading claims.

A half-brother to a dual Group 1-winning sprinter, Gstaad has to be respected on his racecourse debut. Aidan O'Brien's other representative Albert Einstein also warrants consideration on his first start.

Michael Grassick's filly is a strong traveller who will be suited to getting a lead before being produced from off the pace. A winner at the Curragh last time, the daughter of Equiano is 5lb higher. Jorge Alvares adopted similar tactics to win at Dundalk, so supporters will be hoping that they don't cut each other's throats vying for the lead.

With just the three starts to date, the daughter of Kingman is open to any amount of improvement. She is certainly in the right hands to develop into a leading middle-distance horse this season. Tamam Desert is one who could run well at a bigger price.

He can be exprected to have a bright future and could get closest to the selection. Old Is Gold, another pricey breeze-up purchase, and Fitzella look the other likely sorts on paper, with the former just preferred.

selections.comment: ARISAIG would have gone close last time but for a poor trip when short of room up the rail and unable to unleash his final kick. With luck usually a lesser needed commodity here than at the notoriously tricky Goodwood he can gain compensation as conditions look perfect for another top effort. This time he should be able to finish his race off without interference to land the spoils. The unexposed Rainbows Edge is interesting. The Gosden's filly won her first two races (over a mile) last summer before improving again to be runner-up in Listed company when upped to 1m2f. Her prospects look bright but a mark of 99 will not make things easy on season debut up against some seasoned and race-fit rivals and she might have to settle for minor honours. Zapphire could give the selction most to do. A four length defeat on season bow latest is not too inspiring but she needed that and should improve a fair bit for it. She's won on quick ground and likes a stiff finish and shouldn't be far away

selections.comment: The one to take the eye is HICKORY who has posted some of his best efforts in hot handicaps over course and distance, including a fine fourth in last year's renewal of this off a 4lb higher mark before being beaten under 2l in the International Stakes in the summer last year. Jamie Osborne's gelding goes extremely well fresh and has solid claims to get his head in front for the first time since opening his career wit a hat-trick. The dangers are many in such a fiercely competitive heat with the likes of  Myal, Ten Pounds, Roi De France, Pop Master and English Oak all needing serious consideration but at the top of the long list are Metal Merchant, fourth in the Intermnational Stakes over course and distance last year (about half a length in front of the selection but a few pounds worse off) and Qirat, who progressed throughout 2024 and seems to relish the hustle and bustle of big fields, including twice here when 6th of 29 in the Brittania Stakes and 2nd of 18 in the Challenge Cup over course and distance.

selections.comment: TURQUINO makes his handicap debut here protecting an unbeaten record. He's shown signs of greeness both starts but overcame the inexperience and must have a fair bit left in the locker as he gets the hang of things. From a lenient looking mark of 86 the Andrew Balding gelding has a good opportunity of making it three from three on his turf debut. The ultra-consistent Fireblade is most feared. The Frankel gelding opened his account last time having knocked on the door on all five runs since making his debut. That victory came on fast ground at Leicester in early April and he showed a terrific attitude having travelled well. There's likely a bit more progression to come and he'll surely go close. Night Breeze is a serious threat too and is a likely pace-setter. If getting an unpestered lead Ian Williams's gelding could be hard to peg back but Victory Shout may be overlooked and offer a bit more value given he looks primed to hit top form back on turf (winner on fast ground) after a couple of pipe-openers on the AW. Better is expected and he can reward wach-way backers

selections.comment: A small but trappy event with most having some sort of realistic chance. CALEDONIAN is interesting trying this trip for the first time having raced exclusively at 7f as a jujvenile last term. He opened his account on his fourth and final run of 2024 getting rolling close home and shaped as if there's plenty more to come over further. That win probably just about sets the bar on what's been achieved so far by the field and he ran well on first start last year despite greeness and a poor trip so can be expected to be tuned up for this return. Cape Breton is another taking a big step up in trip on season/handicap debut and is feared but Kokanee and Chartwell Jock are feared more. The former, from the Ed Dunlop yard, is a big strapping sort and should come on a bit for his winning start to the campaign and with fitness on his side along with every chance of further progression is taken to go close just ahead of the steadily improving Chartwell Jock who went well on turf/handicap debut in late March and is entitled to be bang there

Back up to ten furlongs and with a run under her belt she's got a good opportunity to add a second win to her CV. Wisper is a massive danger with conditions looking set fair for a near peak effort to kick of her campaign. Alan King's mare won off a layoff in 2022 and 2023 and went close last year and she can repeat the trick to go close here. Aiming High has decent claims but the more unexposed Rock Camelot is feared more having gone well on handicap debut under similar conditoins last time and could have a bit more up her sleeve

Ed Walker's gelding has yet to face ground as quick as it's likely to be today but otherwise has a strong profile for this and should relish the stiff finish having stayed on a bit too late on a few occasions and being a winn er over 7f. Northcliff took a jump forward last time to land a double and must be feared again but there's a suspicion he handled the quirky Brighton track better than most that day and so Dicko The Legend, who has hit greater heights in the past but has been going very nciely on the AW of late and is perhaps better on turf, and Dream Of Mischief, who arrives in fine fettle on the back of a second that kicked of his campaign, are taken to fill the frame. Messafi shouldn't be underestimated and if excused a rare poor effort back on the turf off a break (where the 5f didn't suit) last time. He was showing a bit of progression before that and could reward each way backers

selections.comment: The defeat last time for JIMMY SPEAKING is a bit of concern but he didn't get a clear passage from a wide draw and can be excused that effort given he was placed over the same conditions a few weeks prior. Chris Dwyer's gelding, while prone to the odd blowout, is at least as effective on turf and he's back on his last winning mark achieved here over course and distance last year. Fast ground is no concern and he should go close. Collusion has to prove as effective on fast turf as on artificial surfaces on which he's landed a hat-trick this year and if so will be in the shake-up but Sondad in a first time visor may prove the toughest to crack for the selection. He got back on track second run of the season last time and looks well treated on the pick of his 3yo form. Spanish Star could provide a bit of a surprise having gone well here in the past between 6f and 7f and has not gone on fast ground since winning a class 2 handicap over Epsom's sharp 7f in 2023. The old stalwart can reach the frame

Ki Woo is thriving since encountering good ground following a move from France and is respected on handicap debut having already beaten a rival who ran well at Listed level previously in novices. He can fill the runner up position ahead of Topgun Simmy who beat a couple of useful rivals from top stables in Ireland last week and should remain competitive if turned out quickly.

Harpsichord is guaranteed to stay and, as such, readily preferred to Love Talk for the forecast.

This Irish Derby entry is next best ahead of Prince Of The Seas.

selections.comment: PROTEST RALLY has never won off a mark this high but he's been in career best form this spring and will relish the quick ground here. His draw should allow him to grab the favoured rail and he will be tough to peg back if doing so. Catch Cunningham is tricky to win with but he has been generally consistent on the AW of late and will find this much easier than his turf reappearance. He can fight for a place along with Angle Land who hasn't won in a while but has tumbled down the weights as a result and could surprise at a price.

selections.comment: There are five with a serious chance in this so it is going to be a bit of a shoot-out. Preference is just for NAD ALSHIBA GREEN who was pretty unlucky on her reappearance getting squeezed out and having to switch late. She finsihed well enough to suggest she is better than the bare form and may also come on for that run. Miss Funky Monk is unexposed and progressing and is a big danger. Havana Gila looks on a good mark based on consistent AW form and can go well if showing that here. Military Girl is a terrier in a finish and is another that could be involved while Elegant Erin met trouble in running last time and could step-up and beat the lot of them. Intriguing.

selections.comment: Not much between the trio who all have different profiles. The progressive Serious Chat is unexposed and likely to prove popular after a last time out win on just his second start at 3m. However the thorough stayer may not get the test he needs with STRIKING A POSE likely to get an easy time up front. His strike rate is a concern but he arrives in good form and has won off higher marks in the past. This track suits frontrunners and he can see off both of his rivals. Royal Rhythm is on a fair mark but has big concerns regarding the quick ground and his stamina.
